problems.title: A polynomial-chain derivative at one
problems.question: f(x)=2x³+5(3x−1)²+4. Find f′(1).
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: Power and chain rules give f′(x)=6x²+30(3x−1).
steps: At x=1, the derivative is 6+60=66.

problems.title: A slant asymptote fixes one coefficient
problems.question: For f(x)=(x²+ax+b)/(2−x), find a listed pair a,b whose slant asymptote is y=7−x.
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: Polynomial division gives quotient −x−a−2 and a remainder term tending to zero at infinity.
steps: The constant in the quotient must be 7, so −a−2=7 and a=−9. The remainder can have any b.
The listed pair a=−9,b=11 qualifies.

problems.title: Derivative of complementary inverse functions
problems.question: Differentiate arcsin x+arccos x.
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
steps: The sum is constant, so its ordinary derivative is zero for −1<x<1. The endpoint values do not have ordinary two-sided derivatives.

problems.title: Eccentricity of an ellipse
problems.question: Find eccentricity of x²/9+y²/5=1.
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.

problems.title: An ellipse’s tangent point
problems.question: The line x−3y−12=0 is tangent to x²/36+y²/12=1. Find the contact point.
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: For tangent lx+my=1 to x²/a²+y²/b²=1, contact coordinates are (a²l,b²m).

problems.title: Count extrema of a sine on a short interval
problems.question: How many extrema does sin2x have in (0,3)?
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
steps: The interval contains π/4 and 3π/4, but not 5π/4. Both critical points change derivative sign, so both are extrema.

problems.title: Derivative of a tangent cube
problems.question: f(x)=tan³4x. Find f′(π/16).
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
steps: At x=π/16,4x=π/4, so tan²=1 and sec²=2. The derivative is 24.

problems.title: A plane through a point and parallel to two vectors
problems.question: Find the plane through (1,1,1) parallel to (1,1,1) and (−1,1,2).
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: A normal is their cross product (1,−3,2).
steps: Use (x−1)−3(y−1)+2(z−1)=0. Constants cancel, giving x−3y+2z=0.

problems.title: An equation whose two coefficients vanish
problems.question: The plane Ax+By+Cz+9=0 is parallel to the xy plane. How many roots does Ax=B have?
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: A plane parallel to xy has normal parallel to the z axis, so A=B=0,C≠0.
steps: The equation becomes 0x=0, true for every real x.

problems.title: Tangents from an interior point of an ellipse
problems.question: How many tangents to x²/20+y²/16=1 pass through (1,2)?
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: A point is interior when its normalized square sum is less than 1.
steps: 1/20+4/16=0.3<1, so the point is strictly inside the ellipse. No supporting tangent line passes through an interior point.

problems.title: Differentiate a sine of a product
problems.question: f(x)=sin(xeˣ). Find f′(1).
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: Chain rule and product rule: f′(x)=(eˣ+xeˣ)cos(xeˣ).
steps: At x=1, this equals 2e cos e.

problems.title: A common extremum input for two functions
problems.question: f(x)=x³/3−4x²+7x+5 on [−1,2], and g(x)=3^(x²−ax) on [−2,4]. They attain their maximum and minimum respectively at the same x. Find a.
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
steps: f increases up to x=1 and then decreases on the rest of [−1,2], so its unique maximum is at 1.
g is minimized where its exponent x²−ax is minimized. Its vertex must therefore be at a/2=1, giving a=2. This vertex is within [−2,4].

problems.title: Derivative of a sine cube with a quadratic input
problems.question: f(x)=sin³(x²+π/6). Find f′(√(π/6)).
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
steps: At the input, the angle is π/3. Its sine square is 3/4 and cosine 1/2.

problems.title: A focus of a hyperbola
problems.question: Which listed point is a focus of 9x²−16y²=144?
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
steps: c=√25=5, so the foci are (±5,0). The listed one is (5,0).

problems.title: Distance to a parabola focus
problems.question: For y²=12x, find distance from A=(3,6) to its focus.
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
steps: p=3, so the focus is (3,0). Its distance to A is 6.

problems.title: One extremum versus one stationary point
problems.question: For which a does f(x)=ax³+3x²+x+7 have exactly one extremum?
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: f′=3ax²+6x+1. A genuine cubic has two extrema if this quadratic has two simple real roots, and none if it has a double or no real root.
steps: For a≠0, discriminant 36−12a is positive when a<3, giving two extrema. At a=3 the derivative is (3x+1)², producing a stationary inflection, not an extremum. For a>3 there are none.
At a=0 the function is a quadratic with exactly one minimum. Therefore only a=0 works.
problems.note: No printed choice states only 0. Options combining 0 with 3 or 7 are invalid. The case a=3 has one stationary point but no extremum.

problems.title: Increasing intervals of a quartic
problems.question: Find where f(x)=x⁴/4−2x³/3−5x²/2+6x increases.
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
steps: A sign chart at −2,1,3 gives derivative signs −,+,−,+. The increasing intervals are (−2,1) and (3,∞).

problems.title: Shortest distance between a line and a parabola
problems.question: Find the distance between y=4x−7 and y=x².
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
steps: 4x−x²−7=−[(x−2)²+3], so the distance is [(x−2)²+3]/√17.
The minimum is 3/√17 at x=2.

problems.title: A parallel plane at a given point distance
problems.question: Find the listed plane parallel to x+2y−2z+7=0 and distance 7 from A=(4,3,−2).
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: A parallel plane has equation x+2y−2z+d=0; its normal has length 3.
steps: The variable part at A is 14. Thus |14+d|/3=7 gives d=7 or −35.
d=7 is the given plane itself; the distinct listed parallel plane uses d=−35.

problems.title: A translation preserving a plane
problems.question: Which listed vector translates 2x−3y+5z+7=0 onto itself?
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: A translation preserves a plane iff its vector is perpendicular to the normal.
steps: The normal is (2,−3,5). The listed vector (1,4,2) has dot product 2−12+10=0; the other listed vectors do not.

problems.title: Derivative sign of a decreasing-base logarithm
problems.question: Solve f′(x)≥0 for f(x)=log₀.₃(x²−4).
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
steps: The denominator is negative on the domain, so the derivative is nonnegative exactly when x≤0. Intersecting gives x<−2.

problems.title: A slant asymptote by division
problems.question: Find the slant asymptote of (x²+2x−1)/x.
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
steps: The remainder term tends to zero at both infinities. Thus the asymptote is y=x+2.

problems.title: Number of continuous branches
problems.question: How many continuous branches has x³/(x²−5)?
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: The denominator vanishes at ±√5 and neither zero cancels.
steps: The domain has three connected intervals separated by these two vertical asymptotes. The rational function is continuous on each.

problems.title: An acute plane angle for every parameter t
problems.question: Which listed a admits b such that planes (a−4)x+2y+tz+5=0 and x+bty+tz+9=0 make an acute angle for every real t?
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
steps: This upward quadratic must never vanish, requiring a−4−b²>0. Therefore a>4.
Only the listed a=5 qualifies. Choose b=0: the normals (1,2,t),(1,0,t) have positive dot product 1+t² and are never parallel, so the angle is strictly between 0° and 90°.

problems.title: Two dihedral-bisector planes
problems.question: Planes 2x−2y+z−3=0 and x+2y−2z+12=0 have a bisector plane through their intersection line. Which listed point is its z-axis intercept?
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: Both normals have length 3; equal signed-distance magnitudes give L₁=±L₂.
steps: L₁=L₂ gives x−4y+3z−15=0, whose z intercept is (0,0,5).
L₁=−L₂ gives 3x−z+9=0, with z intercept (0,0,9). Only the first intercept appears in the choices.
